title: GaugeFix-LRM: Function-Preserving Q/K Gauge Fixing for Learnable Multipliers in Language Model Training

contributions.purpose: Control Q/K gauge symmetry drift in Learnable Multipliers without shrinking multiplier magnitudes as weight decay does.
contributions.mechanism: GaugeFix-LRM replaces weight decay on Q/K multipliers with an explicit function-preserving gauge-fixing projection (gauge factor g=sqrt(sQ/sK), rescaling rQ<-rQ/g, rK<-rK*g) that balances Q/K scales while preserving the attention function exactly.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on GPT-2 124M trained on OpenWebText.
contributions.domain: language model training / attention gauge symmetry with learnable multipliers
contributions.source_quote: We propose GaugeFix-LRM, a function-preserving method for controlling Q/K symmetry drift in Learnable Multipliers.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that gauge fixing eliminates Q/K scale drift.
contributions.mechanism: Explicit gauge-fixing projection that balances Q/K scales after each optimizer step.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves perfect drift control (0.000 vs 0.052 baseline), completely eliminating Q/K scale ratio divergence.
contributions.domain: Q/K scale drift control in bfloat16 training
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that GaugeFix achieves perfect drift control (0.000 vs 0.052 baseline), completely eliminating Q/K scale ratio divergence.

contributions.purpose: Explain why pure gauge-fixing can introduce training instability.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis decomposing weight decay's role on Q/K multipliers.
contributions.evaluation: Discovers weight decay serves a dual purpose (symmetry control and magnitude regularization); pure GaugeFix introduces late-training instability in 2 of 3 seeds.
contributions.source_quote: We discover that weight decay on Q/K multipliers serves a dual purpose: symmetry control and magnitude regularization, explaining why pure gauge-fixing can introduce instability.

contributions.purpose: Find the optimal application frequency for GaugeFix.
contributions.mechanism: Applying the gauge-fixing projection every 100 steps rather than every step.
contributions.evaluation: Every-100-steps GaugeFix achieves best validation loss (3.0326), outperforming per-step GaugeFix (3.0711) and the weight decay baseline (3.0633); improves validation loss by 0.0307 nats over baseline.
contributions.source_quote: We show that applying GaugeFix every 100 steps achieves optimal performance, outperforming both per-step application and the weight decay baseline.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We propose GaugeFix-LRM, which replaces weight decay on Q/K multipliers with an explicit gauge-fixing projection.

Learnable Multipliers (LRM) (Velikanov et al., 2026) address this limitation by attaching learnable scalar or vector multipliers to weight matrices... Our work applies gauge-fixing specifically to the Q/K multiplicative symmetry in LRM.

Wang & Wang (2026) characterized the complete gauge group structure, proving that multi-head attention admits (GL(dk))^h x (GL(dv))^h symmetries that persist through LayerNorm. Our work applies gauge-fixing specifically to the Q/K multiplicative symmetry in LRM.

notes: Reports a NEGATIVE side-effect: the function-preserving GaugeFix introduces late-training instability in 2 of 3 seeds; per-step GaugeFix (3.0711) is actually WORSE than the weight decay baseline (3.0633), only the every-100-steps variant beats baseline. Weight decay shown to provide needed magnitude regularization beyond symmetry control.
